Default is deliberately empty rather than a cheap model, unlike the others: Cursor's ids are account- and release-scoped, so a name hardcoded in `cursor_cli.go` reds the whole leg the day the account loses access. Pin a verified id in `e2e.yml` instead. I couldn't pick one — `agent --list-models` needs auth I don't have, and per your notes cursor quota has been out since 08-24.

Checking "every other paid runner has a knob" turned up that it isn't true:

| runner | in-code default | env knob |
|---|---|---|
| codex / gemini / opencode | yes | yes — as you said |
| **claude-code** | `haiku` | **`E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` was documented in CLAUDE.md and read by nothing** |
| **copilot-cli** | `claude-haiku-4.5` | none |
| **droid** | `custom:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | none |
| **cursor-cli** | none | none |

So `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` was a phantom: setting it got you haiku and no warning. Wired it up, plus `E2E_COPILOT_MODEL` (also fixed `copilot-cli.go:407`, where `StartSession` hardcoded the model and would have ignored the new knob — gemini's equivalent at `gemini.go:156` already read `geminiModel()`). Left droid alone: its default is a BYOK custom model that `Bootstrap()` declares in `~/.factory/settings.json`, so a knob moving only the flag would name a model the settings don't declare.

## 2. The five call sites — the numbers weren't the defect, the mechanism was

`runForAgents` (`e2e/testutil/repo.go:435`) already scales the scenario timeout by `TimeoutMultiplier()`. `WithPromptTimeout` didn't, so an absolute number bound hardest on exactly the agents the multiplier exists to give room to. `TestRapidSequentialCommits` asked three commits of gemini in 120s while granting it a 10m scenario budget for being 2.5× slow.

`promptTimeout` now scales the per-test value by the runner's multiplier, **upward only**. The runner's own default and `E2E_TIMEOUT` stay verbatim — the first is already agent-specific and would double-count, the second is typed by a human for one run. Never scaling down is the one asymmetry with the scenario budget: vogon and roger-roger at 0.5× are local and deterministic, so a tighter threshold there could only fire on a loaded machine.

`edge_cases_test.go:138` is the only site that genuinely bounds anything (single prompt): gemini 120s→300s, droid/opencode→240s, codex/copilot/cursor/pi→180s, claude/vogon/roger unchanged. At the two-prompt sites the scenario ctx is the worst-case ceiling either way.

I also strengthened `TestEveryRunPromptResolvesThroughPromptTimeout` to pin that each runner passes *its own receiver* as the scaler — otherwise a runner silently runs on another agent's budget. Negative-tested both branches; messages name the offending expression.

## Three things I found but did not change — your call

- **`multi_session_test.go:47` is self-contradicting.** `promptTimeout := 3 * time.Minute` under `ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, …)` with two prompts: the per-prompt number equals the entire scenario budget, so as written it can never fire for a 1.0× runner. Fixing it means raising the scenario timeout, which raises worst-case CI wall-clock across ten legs — a cost call, not a cleanup.
- **`Claude.StartSession` passes no `--model` at all** (`claude.go:182`), so interactive claude tests run on the account default while its own `RunPrompt` pins `haiku`. Every other runner pins in both paths. Pinning it is a cost win but could red the interactive tests if they lean on a stronger model, and verifying that needs a paid run.
- **`mise-tasks/test/e2e/canary` line 63: `rr_filter="${filter:-TestExternalAgent}"`.** A user filter is applied to roger-roger's lane too, so `canary <any general test>` sends roger-roger at tests CI never runs it against (`e2e.yml:151` scopes it to `TestExternalAgent`). It reported `💥 FAILED (0/3)` for me on a clean tree — same shape as your `codex-integration-test-private-var` note. Unfiltered runs are unaffected. I left it because narrowing that filter changes a shared gate's semantics.

**Verification:** full canary green — vogon 56/56, roger-roger 4/4. `golangci-lint --build-tags e2e ./e2e/...` 0 issues, `go vet -tags e2e ./e2e/...` clean, `mise run fmt` no-op. I proved the roger-roger failures pre-existed by running the same three tests in a throwaway worktree at `86dda0156` — identical results and durations (worktree removed).

for reasons unrelated to the change under test, which is what made the
original 188s measurement unreadable. E2E_CURSOR_MODEL now pins it, applied

drift, and covering StartSession as well as RunPrompt.

E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL had been documented in CLAUDE.md far longer than anything
read it, so setting it got you haiku and no warning; copilot-cli pinned a
default but took no override, and its StartSession hardcoded the model where
gemini's reads geminiModel(). Both are wired up. Droid is deliberately left
alone: its default is a BYOK custom model that Bootstrap() declares in
~/.factory/settings.json, so a knob moving only the flag would name a model
the settings do not declare.

The workflows pin gpt-5.4-nano-medium, measured at $0.0047 per 3-commit
prompt against composer-2.5's $0.0169 (n=3 each, all completing). composer
uses the FEWEST tokens of the candidates and is still 3.6x the dearest,
because it bills cache reads at $0.20/M against nano's $0.02/M and an
agentic loop re-sends the conversation every turn -- so do not rank these by
input price. Nano is the weakest tier offered and only one prompt shape was
probed, so the e2e.yml comment says to bump to gpt-5-mini (same cost, one
tier up) on a capability-shaped failure rather than debug the CLI. There is
no in-code default: `agent --list-models` is account-scoped, and a stale id
exits 1 naming every valid one rather than falling back to `auto`.

scenario timeout. The five call sites were authored when they bound half the
matrix; they now bind all ten, and a duration written in a test file is
authored for the work rather than for whichever runner draws the subtest.

be double-counted, the second is typed by a human for one particular run.

runner passes its own receiver as the scaler. That argument decides how far

multiplier is the same silent drift the guard already existed to catch --
the run still passes, on the wrong budget. Both branches were negative-
tested.

per prompt under a 3m scenario budget with two prompts, so the number cannot
fire as written for a 1.0x runner; and Claude.StartSession passes no --model
at all, running interactive tests on the account default rather than the
haiku its own RunPrompt pins.

Two follow-ups from the prompt-timeout review, plus three adjacent findings I left for a maintainer.

## Cursor pinned no model

`cursor_cli.go` built `agent --force --workspace <dir>` with no `--model`, and the isolated E2E config seeds `cli-config.json` with `{}`, so nothing pinned a model from either direction. Cursor therefore ran on `auto` — a real listed id, and its documented default — which re-routes per run, so turn duration moved for reasons unrelated to the change under test. That is what made the original 188s measurement unreadable.

`E2E_CURSOR_MODEL` now pins it, applied through a shared `cursorArgs()` so the real argv and the artifact's `displayCmd` cannot drift, and covering `StartSession` as well as `RunPrompt`.

Checking the review's premise that "every other paid runner has a knob" showed it was not true:

| runner | in-code default | env knob (before) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| codex / gemini / opencode | yes | yes |
| claude-code | `haiku` | **`E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` was documented in CLAUDE.md and read by nothing** |
| copilot-cli | `claude-haiku-4.5` | none |
| droid | `custom:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | none |
| cursor-cli | **none** | none |

So `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` was a phantom: setting it got you haiku and no warning. It is wired up now, as is `E2E_COPILOT_MODEL` — including `copilot-cli.go`'s `StartSession`, which hardcoded the model where gemini's equivalent already read `geminiModel()`, so the new knob would otherwise have been ignored on that path.

Droid is deliberately left alone. Its default is a BYOK custom model that `Bootstrap()` declares in `~/.factory/settings.json`, so a knob that moved only the flag would name a model the settings do not declare.

## Which model to pin, measured

`gpt-5.4-nano-medium`, per 3-commit prompt, n=3 each, all completing 3/3:

| id | $/run (mean) | range | duration | cache-read tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-5.4-nano-medium` | **$0.0047** | 0.0042–0.0051 | 26.8s (21–30) | 146,773 |
| `gpt-5-mini` | $0.0049 | 0.0046–0.0051 | 35.9s (31–39) | 95,104 |
| `gpt-5.6-luna-medium` | $0.0082 | 0.0079–0.0090 | 23.5s (17–30) | 121,601 |
| `composer-2.5` | $0.0169 | 0.0141–0.0183 | 18.3s (15–21) | 72,276 |

The counter-intuitive part, worth keeping: `composer-2.5` uses the **fewest** tokens of the four and is still 3.6× the dearest, because it bills cache reads at $0.20/M against nano's $0.02/M and an agentic loop re-sends the conversation every turn. Do not rank these by input price, where composer looks merely 2.5× nano.

Token counts come from the CLI's own `usage` block (`agent -p … --output-format json`); prices from [cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing). `cacheReadTokens` was a subset of `inputTokens` in every sample, so cache reads are billed at their own rate; the ranking is unchanged under the other reading.

Nano is the weakest tier Cursor offers and I probed one prompt shape, not the ~50 harder tests in the suite, so the `e2e.yml` comment says to bump to `gpt-5-mini` (same cost, one tier up) on a capability-shaped failure rather than start debugging the CLI. There is deliberately no in-code default: `agent --list-models` is account-scoped, so an id this org is entitled to need not exist for a contributor running the leg locally, and Cursor offers no haiku-tier model at any version to be the obvious cheap choice. A stale pin is safe either way — an unknown id exits 1 naming every valid one rather than silently falling back to `auto`.

## A per-test prompt timeout now scales with the runner

`runForAgents` already scales the scenario timeout by each agent's `TimeoutMultiplier`; `WithPromptTimeout` did not. The five call sites were authored when they bound half the matrix and now bind all ten, so an absolute number bound hardest on exactly the agents the multiplier exists to give room to: `TestRapidSequentialCommits` asked three commits of gemini in 120s while granting it a 10m scenario budget for being 2.5× slow.

`promptTimeout` now scales the per-test value by the runner's multiplier, **upward only**. That asymmetry with the scenario timeout is deliberate: vogon and roger-roger at 0.5× are local and deterministic, so a tighter per-prompt threshold there could only fire on a loaded machine. A runner's own default and `E2E_TIMEOUT` stay verbatim — the first is already agent-specific and would be double-counted, the second is typed by a human for one particular run.

`edge_cases_test.go:138` is the only site that genuinely bounds anything (single prompt): gemini 120s→300s, droid/opencode→240s, codex/copilot/cursor/pi→180s, claude/vogon/roger unchanged. At the two-prompt sites the scenario context is the worst-case ceiling either way.

`TestEveryRunPromptResolvesThroughPromptTimeout` also pins that each runner passes its own receiver as the scaler. That argument decides how far a budget is widened, so a runner handing over a literal or another agent's multiplier is the same silent drift the guard already existed to catch — the run still passes, on the wrong budget. Both branches were negative-tested by breaking a runner deliberately.

## Left for a maintainer, not changed here

- **`multi_session_test.go:47` is self-contradicting.** `promptTimeout := 3 * time.Minute` under `ForEachAgent(t, 3*time.Minute, …)` with two prompts: the per-prompt number equals the entire scenario budget, so as written it cannot fire for a 1.0× runner. Fixing it means raising the scenario timeout, which raises worst-case CI wall-clock across ten legs — a cost call rather than a cleanup.
- **`Claude.StartSession` passes no `--model` at all**, so interactive claude tests run on the account's default model while its own `RunPrompt` pins `haiku`. Every other runner pins in both paths. Pinning it is a cost win but could red the interactive tests if they lean on a stronger model, and checking that needs a paid run.
- **`mise-tasks/test/e2e/canary` line 63 is `rr_filter="${filter:-TestExternalAgent}"`.** A filter you pass to narrow the run is also applied to the roger-roger lane, but CI only ever runs roger-roger against `TestExternalAgent` (`e2e.yml:151`). A filtered canary therefore reports `FAILED (0/3)` on a clean tree; I confirmed it against `86dda0156` in a throwaway worktree before trusting my own diff. Unfiltered runs are unaffected. Left alone because narrowing that filter changes a shared gate's semantics.

## Verification

`mise run check` on the rebased tree with the upstream toolchain (Go 1.27.1, golangci-lint 2.13.2): fmt no-op, lint 0 issues, `test:ci` green including the canary at vogon 56/56 and roger-roger 4/4. `go vet -tags e2e ./e2e/...` clean and both workflow files parse.

The cursor leg itself is **not** verified end-to-end: the model probes above were headless `-p` runs, and the suite uses interactive tmux, where the context is larger — which widens composer's cost disadvantage rather than narrowing it, but does not prove nano completes the harder tests. CLAUDE.md says not to run paid E2E unprompted, so the cursor-cli leg on CI is the first real exercise of the pin.

- `E2E_TIMEOUT` - Per-prompt timeout, overriding each runner's own default (e.g. `E2E_TIMEOUT=4m`)

An unpinned runner re-routes between runs, so turn duration varies for reasons unrelated to the change under test and a single slow measurement cannot be read. Six of the seven paid runners therefore pin a cheap default in code and take an `E2E_*_MODEL` override; `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` pins codex and gemini to cheaper ones still. Two exceptions:

- **Cursor defaults to nothing**, so it runs on `auto` — Cursor's own listed default, which re-routes per run — until `E2E_CURSOR_MODEL` is set. `e2e.yml` and `nightly-e2e.yml` pin `gpt-5.4-nano-medium`, the cheapest id measured at $0.0047 per 3-commit prompt against `composer-2.5`'s $0.0169 — composer is the fastest (18.3s vs 26.8s) but bills cache reads at $0.20/M against nano's $0.02/M, which dominates an agentic loop that re-sends the conversation every turn. Nano is the weakest tier offered, so a capability-shaped failure should be met by bumping to `gpt-5-mini` (same cost, one tier up) before assuming the CLI is at fault. There is deliberately no in-code default: `agent --list-models` is account-scoped (an id this org is entitled to need not exist for a contributor running the leg locally) and Cursor offers no haiku-tier model to be the obvious cheap choice. Not a silent-failure risk either way — an unknown id exits 1 listing every valid one rather than falling back to `auto` — so refreshing the pin from `agent --list-models` is safe.
- **Droid takes no override.** Its default (`custom:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) is a BYOK custom model that `Bootstrap()` declares in `~/.factory/settings.json`, so the flag and that file have to change together — an env knob that moved only the flag would name a model the settings do not declare.

`--model` is passed by both entry points for every runner that pins one, except `Claude.StartSession`, which passes none and so runs interactive tests on the account's default model rather than on the `haiku` its own `RunPrompt` pins.

The per-prompt default is the runner's, not a single number: codex, copilot-cli and gemini use 60s, cursor 90s, opencode 2m, and claude-code, droid, pi, vogon and roger-roger impose no per-prompt bound at all — for those the scenario timeout passed to `ForEachAgent` is the only deadline. `E2E_TIMEOUT` sets a bound for every runner including those, and a per-test `agents.WithPromptTimeout(...)` overrides it. All ten resolve through `promptTimeout` in `e2e/agents/agent.go`; a runner that resolves its own is a build failure (`TestEveryRunPromptResolvesThroughPromptTimeout`), as is one that passes anything but its own receiver as the scaler.

Review findings from Copilot on #2373.

The prompt-timeout scaling in the previous commit assumed WithPromptTimeout

bounds each attempt with it (opencode.go:215), so scaling by opencode's 2.0
turned a documented 90s/30s/30s retry sequence into 180s/60s/60s.

written to enforce -- and broke it silently, since nothing fails, CI just
blocks for longer on the exact path the warmup exists to survive.

The premise behind scaling is false for such a number: it was written by one
runner, for that runner, already knowing how slow it is, so multiplying it by
that same runner's multiplier double-counts. withExactPromptTimeout (unexported)
is now the option for the harness's own deadlines, WithPromptTimeout stays the
scaling one for tests, and TestHarnessDeadlinesAreNotScaled fails the build on
any non-test file in the package that reaches for the wrong one. Negative-tested
by reverting the warmup call site: the guard names opencode.go:215.

which contradicted the very next bullet naming droid as the no-override
exception; it is five (claude-code, codex, gemini, opencode, copilot-cli),
with droid having the default and cursor the override.
